blocks.body: Create a new page from a template, give it a simple file name, and save it in a folder :  not on the desktop.

blocks.heading: What today is
blocks.body: About 90 minutes. Do the lab in the app. The check at the end uses words from today only.

blocks.heading: New page, real folder
blocks.body:
**File > New.** Pick a **DITA Concept** template. A concept is a page that explains what something is. You will meet the other two kinds of pages next week.

Save as `hello-concept.dita` in `oxygen-bootcamp-work/week1/`.

Not the desktop. A file on the desktop gets lost the first time someone looks for `topics/hello-concept.dita`.

blocks.heading: Names
blocks.body: Lowercase. Hyphens. No spaces. `hello-concept.dita` is a good name. `Hello Concept FINAL (2).dita` is how files get lost.

items.title: Word today
items.body: **Template** :  a starter page Oxygen already knows how to edit. File > New attaches the right toolbar. A blank notepad file does not.

items.title: Optional
items.body: **Help > Install new add-ons** has official Live Tutorials inside Oxygen. Nice extra. Not required to finish today.

cards.back: a starter page Oxygen already knows how to edit. File > New attaches the right toolbar. A blank notepad file does not

blocks.title: Getting Started with DITA Using Oxygen XML Editor

lessons.title: A new page in a real folder

blocks.heading: Do the work
blocks.body:
This lab can fail. Fail when: The file is Hello Concept.dita on the desktop, or the title is empty, or the file will not save.

Expected: hello-concept.dita sits in week1/, has a title and a paragraph, and opens again after save.

blocks.intro: Walk the steps in order. Tick them in the lab after you actually do them.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.body: Create a folder oxygen-bootcamp-work/week1/ if it does not exist.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.body: In Oxygen: File > New. Choose a DITA Concept template. (Concept just means “a page that explains what something is.”)

steps.title: Step 3
steps.body: Title: Hello concept. File name: hello-concept.dita :  all lowercase, with a hyphen, not a space.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.body: Save under oxygen-bootcamp-work/week1/, not the desktop.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.body: Under the title, add one short line that says what the page is about. Then add one paragraph in the body.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.body: Confirm Author, Text, and Grid still open this same file.

blocks.summary: hello-concept.dita sits in week1/, has a title and a paragraph, and opens again after save.

blocks.q: Why File > New instead of a blank notepad file?
options: The template sets the page up so the writing toolbar works
File > New publishes the page to the web
blocks.why: A template gives Oxygen the right kind of page. A random .txt file will not get the DITA toolbar.

blocks.q: Which file name will be easier for the rest of the course?
blocks.why: Lowercase, hyphens, no spaces. Other people and later booklets can find it.
